messages:
alex: Heads-up — overnight we saw a spike in tiny-pod PENDINGs in us-west1. Lots of 0.25/0.5 GPU jobs stuck, then mass preemptions when a few big jobs scheduled. Appears to be binpacking fragmentation + latebind churn. graphs: https://grafana/redwood/gpu-pending (short)
sam: Saw that too, +1. evict-rate up ~4x between 02:00-03:30. Small pods getting squeezed out by rack-level packing. Cost estimate ~+7% GPU wasted for the window. :grimacing:
jin: Pulled scheduler logs around 02:12 — a bunch of failed predicates: "InsufficientGPUs" then successful fits after preemption. snippet:
```text
I0312 02:12:07 scheduler.go:345] Rejecting pod/ml-train-xyz: predicate failed: NodeAffinityMismatch
I0312 02:12:09 scheduler.go:512] Preempting pod/ml-batch-987 on node-gpu-122
I0312 02:12:10 scheduler.go:518] Binding pod/large-infer-01 -> node-gpu-200
```
jin: Also saw noisy late-bind behavior: warm pool nodes in us-west1a are being drained too aggressively, causing chain reaction.
ops-bot: alert: evictions/gpu_pod > 200/hour in cluster us-west1 (mar 12 02:10-03:40). Incident ID: INC-20260312-42
lia: Quick thought — our current packing policy prioritizes minimal node count which helps cost but increases fragmentation for variable small-pod mixes. Two options: 1) introduce a tiny-pod class that is allowed to pack tight on a subset of racks, or 2) reserve 1-2 GPUs per rack for tiny jobs (rack-reserve) to avoid global reshuffle. Both have tradeoffs for utilization.
alex: I like option 1 for speed. We can add a scheduler predicate/priority that tags pods with annotation `redwood/pack-class=tiny` and prefer co-locating them. Then allow dev workloads to opt-in. Lower blast radius.
sam: If we do pack-class, we should also add a preemption exclusion window (e.g., 10 min) to avoid immediate evict churn when ephemeral big jobs start. Otherwise pack-class won't help.
jin: Agreed. Implementation sketch:
```yaml
# mark pods
metadata:
  annotations:
    redwood/pack-class: tiny
# scheduler changes
--predicate=PackClassMatch
--priority=PreferPackClass
--preemption-grace=600
```
jin: We'll need admission hook to set redwood/pack-class for known CI/low-priority jobs to avoid human error.
lia: For quick mitigation today: can we bump warm-pool size in us-west1a and reduce early drain frequency? That should lower immediate churn while we design pack-class.
alex: I can roll the warm-pool tweak now (canary us-west1a). Plan: +2 warm nodes, reduce drain concurrency from 5->2. Rolling the change at 03:40.
sam: Please also tag the jobs in the window so we can run retro evals. I'll add a metric: fraction of tiny pods preempted and average time PENDING.
ops-bot: change-request: warm-pool-scale us-west1a +2 by alex at 03:42 — rolling
jin: Post-mortem checklist: collect (1) scheduler bind/preempt timeline for affected pods, (2) node packing heatmap, (3) cost delta. I'll start an eval job to replay the trace on test cluster.
lia: +1 on post-mortem. Also add a backlog task to prototype pack-class and the admission hook.
alex: Action items: alex -> roll warm-pool tweak (in progress), sam -> metrics dashboard patch, jin -> trace replay, lia -> create RFC for pack-class + preemption-grace. We'll revisit tomorrow in infra sync. :thumbsup:
sam: Thx — will post dashboard link once updated.
alex: Update: warm-pool change applied in canary (us-west1a). Monitoring now.
ops-bot: alert cleared: evictions/gpu_pod back to baseline (03:58).
